text:
Student motivation is a major influence on academic achievement. Artificial intelligence can affect motivation by making learning more personalised, interactive, and immediately responsive. However, the same technology may also encourage passive participation and reduce persistence when students become accustomed to receiving instant answers.

AI-supported systems can increase motivation by adapting tasks to the learner’s ability. Students often lose interest when work is either too difficult or too easy. Adaptive platforms can adjust the complexity of questions and provide hints when learners struggle. This may create a more manageable level of challenge and encourage students to continue.

Immediate feedback can also support motivation. In traditional settings, students may wait several days before discovering whether they understood a task correctly. AI systems can respond instantly, allowing learners to correct mistakes while the material is still fresh. Visible progress indicators, personalised goals, and practice recommendations may further help students recognise improvement.

Nevertheless, external support does not automatically create genuine interest. Students may focus on completing AI-generated tasks, collecting scores, or receiving quick praise without developing curiosity about the subject itself. Motivation may become dependent on constant digital stimulation rather than a deeper desire to understand.

Easy access to completed answers presents another risk. Productive struggle is often necessary for learning. When students overcome confusion through effort, they develop confidence and persistence. If AI removes every difficulty immediately, students may become less willing to work through complex problems independently.

Teachers therefore need to design activities that preserve student agency. AI can provide guidance, but learners should still make decisions, explain their reasoning, and reflect on their progress.

AI can improve student motivation when it provides suitable challenges, useful feedback, and clear learning support. However, motivation should not depend entirely on automation. Educational practice must encourage curiosity, resilience, and personal responsibility so that students remain active participants rather than passive users of intelligent systems.
